quizName: Hardest Questions in Indiana Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead at the road for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead to watch for changes in traffic, hazards on the road, and ways to escape danger. Always be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to go faster.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to cross into another lane.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is safe because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Going too fast around a corner may make you cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much alcohol and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Stop them any way you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way home.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly around your head.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces are hard to control on a motorcycle. Which is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal grates are slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can be seen better by:

options.text: Driving very close behind other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Wear bright colors with reflective materials so others can see you. Keep your headlight on, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you correctly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits right when you can reach the ground with your feet while seated. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: What footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Laced-up boots work best. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: When your turn is obvious, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think your intention is obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see. Signals are always required.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for adequate protection while riding.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:
questions.explanation: Securely tuck in your shoe laces so they do not catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who owns a different motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It gives specific information about your bike.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: Which color helps other drivers see you best?
questions.explanation: Bright colors like orange, red, yellow, and green make you easier to see while riding. Wear bright clothing at all times, day or night.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: Do not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
Wear them for a better grip on the handlebars.
Do not wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cold days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear them for a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or other tough gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They are not important because motorcycles are small.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
Use them only when other vehicles are nearby.
They work differently than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use your turn signals when you change lanes or turn, even if no one is nearby.

questions.question: How should you use your mirrors while riding?

options.text: Check them regularly as part of your normal routine.
Avoid checking them because they distract you.
Avoid checking them because other drivers can see you.
Check them only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly as part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Know what is behind you at all times. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine.
